claims.says: When the Dijkstra fast path stops, with source not target, result assembly never panics, a reported path is a minimum-weight walk with the right cost sum, and none means no walk exists.
If the BFS pre-pass for distinct source and target reports no path, every walk from source to target has more than maxLen hops.
Every path the enumeration keeps, at any point of the search, is a simple path from the source, to the target if set, with 1 to maxLen hops, within maxCost, with correct weight and cost.
With pathCount 0 the enumeration terminates; a nonempty answer has valid paths of one minimum weight and every qualifying path of that weight, an empty one means none is within the seed bound.
Converting a JavaScript value that nests deeper than the 1024-level cap back into a FalkorDB value returns an error, on any QuickJS heap, cyclic values included.
